title: State Bank of India v. Deepak Verma
text: The complainant bank filed this case under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act for dishonour of a cheque of Rs 25,00,000 issued by the accused in settlement of an overdue term loan. The cheque was dishonoured on two separate occasions with the remark 'Insufficient Funds'. The complainant issued a statutory demand notice by registered post as required under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Despite service of the notice, the drawer neither paid the cheque amount nor gave any reply. The accused failed to appear despite summons and was tried ex-parte. Documentary evidence including the dishonoured cheque, bank memo, and registered post receipt conclusively establish the ingredients of the offence. The drawer is held guilty under Section 138 NI Act. The court imposes a fine of Rs 50,00,000 and directs payment of the cheque amount to the complainant as compensation. In default, the accused shall undergo two years' simple imprisonment.
